correctness.rationale: At y>0, predator balance gives u+v=sigma. Subtracting per-capita prey equilibrium equations yields (b-a(y))(u-v)=0; monotonic scalar equations classify all predator-positive branches. The s,w,y reduction exactly block-triangularizes the linearization: at the symmetric branch an exchange eigenvalue changes sign at g_c while a Hurwitz quadratic remains; at each prey-exclusion branch its invasion eigenvalue has opposite sign and a strictly Hurwitz tangential quadratic. At g_c the entire line is equilibrium, and the normal quadratic has positive coefficients uniformly as g_c>A*sigma. Symbolic checking of all original-coordinate characteristic factorizations and a rational instance returned CHECK_OK; finite examples are not used as infinite proof. The theorem only asserts local/normal stability.

originality.rationale: The 2024 source (1.7) and its Sections 3–5 were directly inspected, along with the complete equations and relevant theorems of Ahmed et al. (2025) and Mukherjee (2022). The 2024 paper treats nondegenerate isolated internal equilibrium P7 and sufficient Routh–Hurwitz and Lyapunov criteria; it does not state the symmetric coefficient equality, entire predator-positive equilibrium segment, all-point transverse Hurwitz spectrum, or both exclusion-branch stability changes. The other full-text models have distinct predator responses and do not imply the stated result by reduction. Published published-finding corpus semantic results deal with dissimilar flows or symmetry settings. Novelty refers to this exact model-specific theorem, not the general notion of neutral ecological competition.
residual_risks: General results on degenerate competition and neutral manifolds might exist in older or unindexed literature; no claim of exhaustive bibliographic uniqueness.
The result is exactly symmetric, so perturbations can remove the continuum; structural stability under asymmetry is not established.

value.rationale: Fear-dependent self-competition weakens with predator abundance while cross-prey competition stays constant, creating a natural equality at which neutral prey-composition freedom emerges. The theorem identifies the exact threshold, a continuum of predator-positive states, its complete transverse spectrum including endpoints and a stability exchange from coexistence to two exclusion attractors. These distinguish an equilibrium-manifold transition from standard isolated pitchfork/Hopf events and provide a complete sharp local classification across a motivated symmetric parameter family, not a numerical curiosity.
